title: How to Connect Google Sheets to Slack (3 Ways)
description: Post new spreadsheet rows to Slack automatically, comparing Apps Script, Zapier/Make, and a direct webhook setup.
bodyHtml:
There's no first-party Google Sheets-Slack integration, but connecting them is one of the most common lightweight automations teams build: a new row (a form submission, a status change, an order) posts straight into a Slack channel instead of someone having to check the sheet.

MethodSetup effortBest for
Google Apps Script + Slack webhookLow-medium (some scripting)Free, single-sheet automations
Zapier / MakeLowNo-code setup, multiple sheets/triggers
API + backend jobHighHigh volume, custom formatting or filtering logic

Method 1: Apps Script with an onEdit or onFormSubmit trigger

Create a Slack Incoming Webhook in your workspace, then add a script to the sheet (Extensions → Apps Script) that posts to it whenever a row is added:

function notifySlack(e) {
  const row = e.values;
  UrlFetchApp.fetch("https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX", {
    method: "post",
    contentType: "application/json",
    payload: JSON.stringify({ text: `New row: ${row.join(", ")}` })
  });
}

Attach it as an installable trigger ("On form submit" or "On edit") from the Triggers panel. This is free and has no external dependency, but you own the script and its error handling.

Method 2: Zapier or Make

Use the "New Spreadsheet Row" trigger (polls on an interval, typically 1-15 minutes depending on plan) and a "Send Channel Message" action. No scripting required, and it's easy to add filters (e.g. only post if a "Status" column equals "Approved").

Method 3: API + backend job (for developers)

For high-volume sheets or custom formatting logic beyond what Apps Script or Zapier support cleanly, pull rows with the Google Sheets API from a scheduled job and post to Slack with the Web API or a webhook. This is the right call once you need retries, batching multiple rows into a single digest message, or de-duplication logic.

Which to pick

Apps Script is the fastest free option if you're comfortable pasting a short script in. Zapier/Make is faster still if you'd rather not touch code. Go custom only once volume or logic complexity outgrows both.
